clue.text: In control, buttoned up, opener takes leg guard

parts.note: a key is the thing that opens a lock
a pad is the protective guard a cricketer straps to the leg

explanation.surface: A tense, tightly buttoned batsman takes the first over and straps on his pads.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words read like a cricketer's temperament, but together they describe the device: a panel of buttons used to key in commands. A cricket PAD protects a batter's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A keypad is an input control made of pressable buttons, as on a phone or alarm panel.

clue.text: Start off from lower number

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off

parts.note: nether means lower

explanation.surface: Begin by subtracting from a smaller figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs; ether is an old anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was used as an anaesthetic, so it is a number: something that makes you numb.

clue.text: I chop up incomplete binder: some such secret?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lop is to chop

indicators.note: the last letter is missing

parts.note: cement binds bricks together

explanation.surface: Someone cuts up a half-finished folder, hiding a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I + LOP to POLI; 'incomplete' cuts CEMENT to CEMEN. Secret police are the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: The secret police are a force of policemen, so policemen are some of such a secret body.

clue.text: Boy raised to accept doctrine that describes economic science

indicators.note: the boy takes the doctrine inside him
in a down clue, raised means read upwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
an ism is a doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: A lad is brought up to believe a creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LAD to DAL, which holds ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle called economics 'the dismal science', so this adjective describes it.

clue.text: Extravagant manner, going off to the barracks

parts.note: food that is going off smells high, gamey or starting to rot
a camp is a place where soldiers are quartered, like barracks

explanation.surface: Someone flounces off to the army quarters in theatrical style.
explanation.definitionFit: High camp is a deliberately exaggerated, theatrical style of behaviour or presentation.

clue.text: Saintly type, member of Dail, one with tiny electorate

parts.note: holy means saintly
roman is the upright printing type

indicators.note: the member belongs inside the Irish body

parts.note: the Dail is the parliament of Eire, Ireland
MP is short for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A pious person, a deputy in the Irish parliament, has very few voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saintly type' looks like one person, but splits in two. The emperor was chosen by only a handful of princes, the Electors; the Dail is Ireland's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Roman Empire's ruler was elected by a few princes, so it had a tiny electorate.

clue.text: American chap has a relaxed manner of speaking

parts.note: a guy is a chap

indicators.note: said out loud, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an ease is a relaxed manner, spoken as 'an ease'

explanation.surface: A US fellow talks in a laid-back way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. 'American' suggests the USA, but the person is from Guyana in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is in South America, so a native of it is an American in the continental sense.

clue.text: Blow to maintain constant pressure round chimney .

indicators.note: the constant and pressure are placed around the chimney

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, as the speed of light
P is the symbol for pressure
lum is a Scots and northern word for chimney

explanation.surface: A gust keeps up steady pressure round the smokestack.
explanation.definitionFit: A clump is a heavy blow, as a clumsy punch.

clue.text: Tart ingredient, tame recipe?

parts.note: the word tame is a recipe for the minced word meat: mix its letters and tame results

explanation.surface: A mild cookery recipe for a pastry filling.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, mince 'meat', gives TAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the spiced fruit filling of mince pies and tarts.

clue.text: Youngster turned out to be no problem

parts.note: a child is a youngster
to splay is to turn or spread outwards, as feet that are splayed

explanation.surface: A child grows up to cause nobody any trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is child's play is extremely easy, so it presents no problem at all.

clue.text: Our men welcomed aboard American vessels

indicators.note: the Americans take our men onto their ship, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is the British setter's own sailors

explanation.surface: British sailors are greeted as they step onto US ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vessels in the sense of containers, such as vases or tea urns.

clue.text: I march right round front of Arthur's Seat

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker climbs round Arthur's Seat, the hill overlooking Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is an Edinburgh hill, which steers away from furniture. 'round' rearranges IMARCH plus R into RMCHAIR, placed after A from the front of Arthur's.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a seat with supports for the arms.

clue.text: Place one's dying to see?

parts.note: plays on the saying 'see it and die', made of the Italian city on its bay: a place you must see before you die

explanation.surface: A bucket-list destination someone is desperate to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'See Naples and die' claims nothing after it could match the view of the city; the clue turns 'dying to see' from eager wish into literal order.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is the Italian city of the saying that once you have seen it you may die content.

clue.text: Live beside jolly narrow path

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone lives cheerfully beside a slender footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but crossword setters use it for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A berm is a narrow ledge or path, such as one beside a canal or along a bank.

clue.text: Recommend from court, forgetting outside, to be put into jail

indicators.note: the trimmed court goes inside the jail word

parts.note: to encage is to jail or lock up

indicators.note: the outer letters are dropped, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A judge sends someone from court to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting outside' strips court's first and last letters; 'to be put into' sets what is left inside the jail word.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone to do something is to recommend or urge it.

clue.text: A glass of it giving inspiration shortly to trainee?

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a muse is a source of inspiration
a cadet is a trainee in the forces or police

explanation.surface: A drink gives a young recruit a little creative boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the last letter of the inspiration. The definition is unusual: the 'it' of a glass of it is the wine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire, something poured by the glass.

clue.text: King has talent to waste

indicators.note: the letters are laid waste and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch squanders his gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to waste' rearranges HAS TALENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Athelstan was a tenth-century Anglo-Saxon king, the first king of all England.

clue.text: Scatty tricks I'd picked up have appeal

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: arts are tricks or wiles
I'd is written as ID
it is sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: Scatterbrained schemes someone has learned turn out to be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns ARTS + ID together into DISTRA; 'have' is a link to IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means absent-minded or distracted, which is scatty.

clue.text: Quick look: nothing wrong about analysis of poem

parts.note: to scan is to glance over quickly

indicators.note: the wrong goes around the nothing, holding it inside

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A glance at a poem finds nothing to criticise in the analysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Scansion is the analysis of the metrical pattern of a line of verse.

clue.text: Shelter posh African

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter
U stands for upper-class, a label for posh speech and manners

explanation.surface: A smart African takes cover.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from the British debate over 'U and non-U' usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a Hutu is an African.

clue.text: Group has right to eat meal

indicators.note: the group holds right within it

parts.note: a bunch is a group

explanation.surface: The party is entitled to have a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: In shock, with a temperature? Isn't one bright-eyed and bushy-tailed?

parts.note: someone in shock is numb

explanation.surface: A feverish patient in shock is hardly lively and alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bright-eyed and bushy-tailed' usually means alert, but here it describes a real animal with a bushy tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbat is an Australian marsupial with a long bushy tail and alert eyes.

clue.text: Curb ambition to entertain film star

indicators.note: the clue words hold the answer inside, as a host entertains a guest

explanation.surface: Rein in your hopes of hosting a movie celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the deer who stars in the Disney animated film named after him.

clue.text: Streaky lines spoil jewellery

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Ugly streaks ruin a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbling is a pattern of streaks like the veins in marble, as in meat or endpapers.

clue.text: Feature with hole in middle: head could go in it

indicators.note: the hole goes into the centre of the feature

parts.note: a nose is a facial feature
O is a hole by its shape

explanation.surface: A face with a hole in the centre that a head fits through.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop, as on a hangman's rope, into which a head could be put.

clue.text: Train gun on mark and hurt badly

parts.note: M is short for mark, the former German currency
to aim is to point or train a gun at a target

explanation.surface: A soldier points a gun at a target and badly injures someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to wound someone so badly that they are permanently injured.

clue.text: Brecht's effect conveys no truth to people

parts.note: something with no truth is a lie, A LIE
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A playwright's technique delivers falsehood to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Brecht's alienation effect keeps the audience at a critical distance from a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The alienation effect is the distancing technique the playwright Brecht used in his theatre.

clue.text: Disparage prime minister, powerless in beauty's embrace

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the beauty's arms
the beauty's embrace surrounds the other piece, holding it within

parts.note: a belle is a beauty

indicators.note: without power, so the P (power) is removed

parts.note: Pitt, father and son, were British prime ministers

explanation.surface: A weakened premier is mocked while in the arms of a beautiful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' removes P (power) from the prime minister; William Pitt is the premier meant, and 'in ... embrace' puts what is left inside the beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle is to disparage, making someone seem small or unimportant.

clue.text: Female about to scream no end, rowing here

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters run backwards
with no end, the last letter goes

parts.note: to yell is to scream

explanation.surface: A woman is about to shriek, with no end to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts YELL to YEL, and 'about' turns that to LEY. Henley-on-Thames hosts a famous regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Henley is the Thames town famous for its rowing regatta.
